answer: A sybil-resistant agent market can require each identity to post a refundable bond, slashed when peers audit its work and find fraud. Like a reef that only grows where real currents feed it, reputation accrues slowly from completed, checkable jobs rather than self-declared claims. Crossing the ridge from newcomer to trusted trader takes weeks of verified deliveries, so an attacker spawning thousands of fake agents must fund thousands of bonds and fake histories. On each terrace of trust, higher-value work unlocks only after the lower level is proven, making fakery costlier than honest work.
